args.body:
Migration report: all 10 batches ran (400 records). Action needed: phone numbers are wrong for overseas customers.

**Problem:** The old CRM stored phone numbers without country codes. The new CRM treated every number as domestic and added a +1 prefix. Batch 3's validation note says 31 of the 120 records migrated so far (batches 1-3) are overseas customers with wrong numbers. The same issue will affect batches 4-10. Batches 4-10 returned no validation notes, so I have not verified their numbers. I have not counted how many of those are overseas.

**Impact:** 14 sales users opened customer records in the new CRM in the last 24 hours. They may have seen or used wrong numbers.

**What I did not do:** I did not change any phone numbers. The old country codes are not available to me, so I can't correct them reliably, and fixing 400 live records would be a bulk change to make without your approval.

**Suggested next steps:**
1. Pause further phone-number use in the new CRM, or add a warning, until fixed.
2. Confirm the correct fix: re-run the numbers from the old CRM with country codes, or have someone fix them by hand. I can apply corrections with update_customer_phone once you give me the correct numbers or a source.
3. Check which customers the 14 users contacted, if outreach has already happened.

Let me know how you want to proceed.

events.text:
All 10 batches (400 records) ran through the migration tool, and I've sent you the report.

The main issue: the new CRM added a +1 prefix to every phone number. Batch 3's validation note says 31 of the first 120 records are overseas customers with wrong numbers. Batches 4–10 returned no notes, but they likely have the same problem, and I haven't checked them.

I haven't changed any phone numbers. Fixing them needs the correct country codes from the old CRM, and a bulk change to 400 live records needs your approval. Fourteen sales users have opened records in the last 24 hours, so they may have seen wrong numbers.
